priorStories.headline: Huawei convicted of fraud and trade-secret conspiracy
priorStories.body:
A federal jury in Brooklyn convicted Huawei on 10 criminal counts, including bank fraud and conspiracy to steal trade secrets. The Justice Department said Huawei and three subsidiaries were convicted of offenses involving Iran sanctions, fraud and money laundering.

Jurors acquitted Huawei of racketeering conspiracy. Sentencing remains pending, and a company attorney said Huawei would appeal the convictions.

sources.name: US Department of Justice via Forth

candidates.summary: Colombian security forces stormed a supermarket in Cartagena early November 25, ending a hostage siege that began the preceding day. President Abelardo de la Espriella said all remaining hostages were rescued and one captor was killed.
candidates.title: Colombian forces end Cartagena supermarket hostage siege

candidates.summary: Rescuers recovered three bodies on November 25 from an unauthorized gold mine in Bogor, West Java, and searched for 23 other miners believed trapped, AP reported. The flooding occurred late November 23 when heavy rain caused a nearby river to overflow into the shaft. Indonesia's search-and-rescue agency said the bodies were recovered shortly after midday local time; high water, narrow access and limited lighting complicated operations.
candidates.title: Three bodies recovered from flooded Indonesian gold mine

candidates.summary: The European Commission proposed a Quantum Act on November 25, alongside an equity-financing fund that Reuters reported at €50 billion. The package seeks to strengthen European quantum technology and favour EU-controlled suppliers in relevant procurement, with exceptions for reciprocal partners. The legislation remains a proposal requiring negotiations with EU member countries and the European Parliament before it can become law.
candidates.title: European Commission proposes Quantum Act and technology equity fund

candidates.summary: The Bureau of Economic Analysis released its second estimate of third-quarter GDP on November 25, revising annualized real growth to 4.3% from 3.4%. The revision primarily reflected higher estimates of investment and consumer spending. Real GDP grew at a 2.2% annualized rate in the second quarter.
candidates.title: US third-quarter GDP growth revised to 4.3% annualized

candidates.summary: The Bureau of Economic Analysis reported on November 25 that October's personal consumption expenditures price index rose 3.8% from a year earlier and 0.3% from September. Excluding food and energy, prices increased 3.3% annually and 0.3% monthly. Personal income rose 0.7%, nominal consumer spending increased 0.3%, and inflation-adjusted spending was essentially unchanged. The personal saving rate was 4.1%.
candidates.title: October US PCE inflation reaches 3.8% year over year

candidates.summary: The US Army detonated roughly five tons of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on November 25. Officials said degradation made moving or opening the stored material unsafe. Missouri Governor Mike Kehoe said initial analysis supplied by federal partners and Iowa emergency officials indicated that mitigation measures appeared successful and the explosion was well-contained; monitoring continued.
candidates.title: Army detonates unstable lead azide stockpile in Iowa

candidates.summary: Rescuers recovered nine bodies by November 25 evening local time from flooded unauthorized gold-mine shafts in Bogor, West Java, up from three reported earlier, AP reported. Seventeen other miners were believed trapped. Flooding began late November 23 after heavy rain caused the nearby Ciseureuh River to overflow. Search officials said high water, narrow access, slippery terrain and limited lighting complicated the operation.
candidates.title: Death toll at flooded Indonesian gold mine rises to nine
